newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Skandia's AFS to have new structure in 12.
newsitem.headline: Skandia's AFS to have new structure in 12.

text.p: Swedish insurer Skandia Insurance Co Ltd said on Wednesday its unit linked assurance operations, Assurance & Financial Services (AFS), would have a new structure within 12 to 18 months.
Then, the company could decide whether or not to spin off AFS and list it separately.
"The AFS board has taken affect today and it will take a few years to go through the legal structure of the company," Skandia's chief executive Lars-Eric Petersson told a news conference.
He emphasised that such a structural review was made in all of Skandia's companies.
"We will increase the lucidity of financial data, market prerequisites, threats and possibilities," Petersson said. "The same focus as for listed companies."
He did not want to disclose what would happen to AFS after the new structure was in place.
"First we will do this job and then we will make an estimate of what is best for the shareholder in the long term," he said.
When asked if the "long-term best" was the same thing as a spin-off, he said: "Why is it so sure that a spin-off (of AFS) is the best thing for shareholders?"
